summary: 1. Key operational findings Oct 12 posted 22,351 BCM against a 24,072.2 BCM target (-7.15%), a smaller miss than Oct 11's -23.50%, at day 18 of the 30-day fiscal cycle (12 days remaining). 2. MTD narrowed slightly to 365,676 BCM against 397,191.6 (-7.93%), the first improvement in four days after Oct 9's -6.85%, Oct 10's -6.91% and Oct 11's -7.98%. 3. Three things to flag: 1. 4. The split between waste and ore flipped sharply: waste missed by 29.44% (13,857 vs 19,637.3 BCM) while ore ran 91.52% over target (8,494 vs 4,435.0 BCM), the sharpest ore-over/waste-under split of the cycle, pulling the day's stripping ratio down to 1.63 from Oct 11's 5.00. 2. 5. The crusher logged its second straight zero-feed day (0 BCM, planned maintenance shutdown that began Oct 11); MTD throughput sits at 9,753 LCM against a 74,400 LCM plan (13.11%, down from Oct 11's 13.88%), with no reopening date given yet. 3. 6. Three excavators were down simultaneously for the first time this cycle: EX-253 and EX-263 on their standing faults (day 27 and day 8) plus EX-247 newly down 11 hours for a planned 1,000-hour service; a data-quality flag also opened on dump truck DT-346, which logged a full 24-hour "down" status against only a routine daily-inspection entry with no closing time recorded. 7. Fleet availability (Daily Availability Final Report, authoritative over the A&U workbook): excavators 63.69% day / 66.00% MTD, the weakest daily excavator reading logged this cycle; trucks 86.25% / 90.54%; drills 93.23% / 86.15%; overall 87.50% / 86.92%, core fleet 81.46%. 8. Lost volume: excavators (EX-253, EX-263, EX-247) 19,140 BCM / 51,678 t gross; dump trucks (DT-107, DT-108, DT-110) 4,348 BCM / 11,740 t — combined 23,488 BCM / 63,418 t, well above the day's 1,721 BCM target miss, confirming trucks rather than diggers set the day's pace. 9. WL-329's cutting-edge changeout, flagged open on Oct 11 after a 4.5 h breakdown, closed out after an 11.25 h GET changeout and bucket-weld repair spanning 11-Oct 11:45 PM to 12-Oct 4:45 PM. A new fault opened on WT-300 (water truck), down 22.25 h on a tyre puncture from 7:15 AM. Survey reading for Oct 12 production (261013-INX-SUM): trucks 22,351 BCM vs survey 23,093 BCM, +742 BCM (+3.21%) — survey back above trucks after Oct 11's single negative day. Cumulative gap narrows to -28,649 BCM (-8.50%) from -29,391 BCM (-9.36%). Survey MTD crosses the halfway mark for the first time this cycle at 50.91% of the 661,986 BCM monthly target; the daily rate needed from Oct 14 rises to 27,079.92 BCM, the steepest ask of the cycle so far. The A&U, DPR, Drill Meters, Drill Sampling, Equipment Running Hours, Running Hours Maaden, Distance Report and Grade Control Sheet workbooks gained Oct 12 tabs but were registered by name only, not deep-read (the Client Meeting Report and the Daily Availability Final Report cover the figures compiled this pass). DT-346's anomalous down-status entry and EX-247's day of "no jobs" standby even in its nominally-available hours are flagged as open questions, not resolved. The mineable-area PDF and the broken-stock email's inline-image table remain unread, consistent with prior passes. `publish_insights.py` was deliberately not run this pass — the `wiki-insights-sync` task publishes separately at 11:00/17:00. Source: KNOWLEDGE/mining_operations_kb/RAW via the librarian compile protocol.
